beats.headline: Choo Choo
beats.text: The party lands in a hurtling subway car, Mongo screeching in anger and fear, Donut trembling on Carl's shoulder, Katia clutching a pole, and the System greets them with an achievement: I'm on a train! Choo Choo, Motherfucker. The reward is a Train Conductor's Souvenir Hat. Wear it with pride! Getting dressed in the car, Carl briefly examines his, and it is junk. It is not magical. It is a simple, blue and white hat of the kind one would see on a toddler, with the words I rode the Iron Tangle embroidered on it.

beats.headline: The stupid hat was a key
beats.text: Going down the stairs from the abyss, Carl sorts his inventory by the items the portal has marked, and finds three keys to it: the Ochre Key, the Steam Train Key, and that stupid souvenir hat. Holy shit. All they needed to do was equip the hat. He messages everybody on his chat list: equip the hat, ride a train to the end of the line, and you will get through, though the train car will not, and you will land in a station full of thousands of zombies. Mei W answers that her whole party sold theirs. They were offering five thousand gold each.

beats.headline: No hat, no way out
beats.text: Bautista sends an update. They tried to paralyse the Kravyad, she ended up dying, and the portal closed. Over 150 of them do not have their souvenir hats, the trains have stopped coming on all the tracks, and they are heading for the abyss portal on foot, about fifty kilometres. Does he have a hat, Carl asks. Nope. A guy at the bar was bragging about how much they were buying them for, and a bunch of them sold. Dumb. Get to the abyss, Carl tells him, and send those who have hats through on foot.

beats.headline: Seven hundred in twenty minutes
beats.text: With people trapped at the end of the line, the plan is to take the battered Vermillion car all the way there and hand out as many hats as possible. At station 75 Carl trades fist bumps and loudly asks for people's hats and any keys they have gathered. They are standoffish at first; once they learn why, they coordinate and spread the word, and in twenty minutes he has over 700 hats and fifteen keys. Donut whispers that they could sell them for over three million. The System awards him Mentally Unstable Clothing Hoarder, and declines to reward the behaviour. It's weird.

beats.headline: Plan C, and a tribute
beats.text: Carl changes the plan: he has enough hats in his inventory for everybody, so they go through the abyss portal and skip the mimic waiting at the cart portal. Donut wants the hats back afterwards. Millions of gold, Carl. He tosses thirty on the ground behind the cart for stragglers, puts his own on, and they go through. Then Bautista takes his off and sets it in front of Donut. For you, Princess Donut. A line forms, each crawler bowing and dropping the stupid train hat in tribute. It was Katia's idea. Donut gathers them all into her inventory, tail swishing.

beats.headline: Not for a single gold
beats.text: The whole group is waiting at the open stairwell for them. Carl, Carl, Donut cries as they approach: we never tried to sell my hats! Carl had, actually, tried to sell one while she was in the training room. The proprietor laughed at him and said nobody was buying them any more. Not even for a single gold. He hasn't the heart to tell her. They will try on the next floor, he says.

beats.headline: Luca Di
beats.text: An entry in Donut's A Banquet Fit for a Princess is Luca Di's: a human Pastamancer, final level 62. You probably don't remember me, Princess, it begins, but I was one of the ones to give you my train hat on the fourth floor. She saved his life, he writes, and the life of his mother, Giulia DiMarco, as well. They never got along when he was growing up, and when her dementia came they placed her in a home. Guilt finally got the best of him, and he went to visit her on that day.
